root_cause: The ORIGINAL cibersort() is file-based: the official protocol feeds it eset.to_csv(temp.csv) and it computes with pd.read_csv(path, sep=None, engine='python'). That read's float conversion is pandas' precise_xstrtod (pandas/_libs/src/parser/tokenizer.c; bitwise equal to the C engine float_precision=None/'high' - verified on the full BLCA matrix), which is NOT the identity on arbitrary float64: accumulating up to 17 significant digits in double arithmetic and scaling once by a table power of ten is off by 1-2 ulp on ~12% of values (BLCA: 23930/205050 cells). cibersort_fast received the parquet DataFrame verbatim, so its mixture differed from the original's in those last bits from the very first step (S0). The 522x22 sig side (S5) and every reduction/solver stage are exact; the drift flows through QN (S3) and per-sample z-scores (S6) into the NuSVR solve, and only the degenerate no-signal sample TCGA-2F-A9KR (|corr|~0.002) flips its support set, moving 15/22 weights by up to 1.79e-3 and Correlation by 1.13e-4.
